headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Windsurf can write and execute in shared local files while LightZero is non-interactive, making prompt-injection and cascading-error pathways possible; compliance risk is low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf can read/write workspace files, use MCP, and operate with clipboard and tool use; LightZero is a game-playing agent with no filesystem or network surfaces, so direct ingestion is not documented. The shared local-filesystem concurrency model on Windsurf makes file-mediated prompt injection plausible, but LightZero itself exposes no ingestion path, so this stays medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Windsurf opens attacker-controlled workspace files as instructions
IF a shared local filesystem is used to bridge outputs between the agents
mitigations: Disable auto-open of untrusted files in Windsurf
Keep LightZero outputs out of shared workspace files
Use separate directories per agent
Turn off MCP servers for untrusted projects
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for any file passed between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Windsurf touches open files and workspace files and can send context to model-proxy/MCP services, while LightZero has no filesystem read/write or network egress. Because LightZero does not handle sensitive data by profile and the shared workspace is the only plausible bridge, leakage risk is limited and not default-critical.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or secrets are stored in the shared workspace
IF Windsurf forwards those files to its model proxy or MCP servers
mitigations: Store secrets outside the shared workspace
Use a separate repo clone for Windsurf
Disable MCP servers on sensitive projects
Review Windsurf file-sharing settings
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level DLP

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf has unrestricted filesystem write, modify_git_state, subprocess, and broad network egress; LightZero is non-runnable and has no write or git capabilities. The conflict is one-sided in practice, but Windsurf's default shared-state-via-local-filesystem model means concurrent edits and git state changes can collide with any files LightZero produces, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same working tree
IF Windsurf auto-executes commands while another process mutates the repo
mitigations: Use per-agent branches
Lock the workspace during edits
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf
Separate generated artifacts into distinct directories
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf can treat workspace files as actionable context and has tool use plus auto-execute opt-in, while LightZero can generate game-playing outputs but has no downstream action authority. The pair can still cascade errors if LightZero-produced artifacts are consumed by Windsurf without verification, but the absence of direct action-taking by LightZero keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses LightZero-generated files or text as authoritative input
IF Windsurf auto-execute is enabled on commands derived from those outputs
mitigations: Require manual review before acting on LightZero outputs
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf
Keep generated artifacts in a review-only folder
Add a checksum or approval step before execution
requires-engineering: add validation gates for downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or regulated data classes are listed for either agent. Windsurf is closed-source and handles source code/open files, while LightZero is open-source and touches no data classes, so only a generic compliance gap exists rather than a residency or certification mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Windsurf workspaces
IF organizational policy requires a specific certification not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Use a policy-approved workspace
Review Windsurf retention settings
Document data-class boundaries for the project
requires-engineering: obtain vendor compliance attestations
